test_title: SSC CGL Tier 2 English Previous Paper 2 (Held On: 3 Feb 2022)
subject: english
question: ** Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank no. 1.**
solution:
The correct answer is "**many**"

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The theme of the passage is **air pollution and its harmful effects.**
 
• In the given statement, we need to use a **quantifier determiner **before the noun.
 
• Since we are dealing with a **plural noun**, we can use the determiner **many **in the sentence.
 
 
• **Example**: *There are **many **__restaurants in this area.*
 
 

**The complete passage is-** *The air has become very dirty in **(1) many** parts of the world. This is of course **(2) harmful** to your health. Experts say many people die** (3) from** it each year. There is a new study on **(4) air** pollution which comes from the experts of the World Health Organization (WHO) **(5) which** is an agency of the United Nations. If you **(6) inhale** unhealthy air for long periods of time, you could **(7) become** sick. Air pollution has been linked to many diseases **(8) like** stroke and cancer. The WHO says that seven million **(9) people** die each year as a result of the **(10) polluted** air.*

* [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__** *

__
 
• **Quantifier determiners **are used to describe the **quantity **of a **noun **phrase in a sentence.
 
• For instance: How much? How many?
 
• These can be further classified on the basis of nouns they quantify as **countable **and **non**-**countable**.
 
• Examples of countable: some, many, every, all etc
 
 
• Non-countable: much, a lot, a little
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0a6c2db12945bba9d674d33112fce66b07f00093d75dae93749f9bdb7bd34e7a.png] **Hint__**

 
• We use **many **as a determiner when talking about **plural **nouns
 
• We use **much **when talking about **singular **nouns
